image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a bison's head and upper forequarters against a snowy background. The bison has thick, dark brown shaggy fur, a prominent shoulder hump, and a visible horn curving upward. The eye is dark and alert. The lower jaw features a beard of long hair. One front leg is partially visible, appearing sturdy and covered in fur.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large broad head with short curved horns.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visibly large and broad relative to the frame. A short, curved horn is clearly visible on the side facing the camera.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beard of long hair on chin and throat.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct long, shaggy hair hangs from the chin and throat area, matching the description of a bison beard.
The visible eye is dark and well-defined.
The ear is small and largely obscured by the thick surrounding fur, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Massive body with exceptionally tall, heavily built proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop focusing on the head and neck; the full body proportions and withers height cannot be fully assessed relative to the whole animal.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Shaggy dark brown fur covering forequarters forming prominent shoulder hump.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fur is visibly shaggy and dark brown. The curvature of the neck into the shoulder suggests the characteristic hump, though the full extent is cropped.
The hindquarters are completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short horns compared to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the horn is visible, the 'body size' reference is missing due to cropping, making a comparative judgment impossible.
Only the upper part of one front leg is visible; the lower leg and hooves are not in the frame.
The tail is not visible in this head-and-shoulders shot.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness and minor blending/bleeding where the dark fur meets the bright white snow, particularly around the chin beard. This is common in AI generation but could also be depth-of-field blur. It lacks the sharp crispness of a high-end photograph.

The transition from the horn to the skull appears slightly smoothed and indistinct. The texture of the horn merges somewhat abruptly with the fur without a clear biological boundary or skin line, suggesting a minor generative fusion.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species classification and rule out hybrid artifacts (e.g., cow-bison mix).
To analyze the subtle edge bleeding and texture consistency of the shaggy fur against the snow.
To verify the structural integrity and boundary sharpness between the horn and the skull/fur.

focus_areas: Fur edge sharpness against high-contrast snow
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the horn base. In AI images, horns often 'melt' into the fur rather than emerging from a distinct pedicle. Check if the fur texture remains consistent or if it becomes 'smudged' near the horn. Also, evaluate if the eye has a realistic catchlight or if it looks like a flat black dot.
